# Session 5: Reaching the Python ecosystem

## Objectives

By the end of this session, students can:

- Import a real Python callable with `extern` and give it a Pyfun type, using `extern pure` where a
  call is genuinely side-effect free.
- Decode untrusted JSON into a typed record or a structured error with the `Decode` module.
- Rewrite a staircase of `Result` matches as a flat `result { }` computation expression using `let!`
  and `return`.
- Tag a number with a unit of measure and let the compiler check dimensions, then explain that units
  erase at lowering.
- Group definitions into a module and qualify calls as `Module.member`.
- Assemble a small end-to-end pipeline that decodes, folds, and computes a unit-checked result.

## Prerequisites

Sessions 1 through 4. The capstone leans on records (Session 3), `Result` and `match` (Session 2),
and folds (Session 3), so this session is best after the whole unit.

## Six-session variant

If you are running the unit as six sessions, split here. Session 5 becomes lessons 12 and 13 (extern
and decoding, then computation expressions), and Session 6 becomes lessons 14 through 16 (units,
modules, and the capstone), with the capstone as the finale. The demo script below is ordered so the
split falls cleanly after step 4.

## Demo script

The thread is the boundary versus the engine: Pyfun earns its keep where the outside world is untyped
and can fail, and it stays out of the way of fast native code.

1. Open the [Lesson 12 exercise](https://simontreanor.github.io/Pyfun/playground/#code=dHlwZSBCb29rID0geyB0aXRsZTogc3RyaW5nLCBwYWdlczogaW50IH0KCmxldCBib29rRGVjb2RlciA9CiAgRGVjb2RlLm1hcDIgKGZ1biB0aXRsZSBwYWdlcyAtPiBCb29rIHsgdGl0bGUgPSB0aXRsZSwgcGFnZXMgPSBwYWdlcyB9KQogICAgKERlY29kZS5maWVsZCAidGl0bGUiID90aXRsZURlYykKICAgIChEZWNvZGUuZmllbGQgInBhZ2VzIiA_-IGRlc2NyaWJlIHw-IHByaW50Cm1pc3NpbmdGaWVsZCB8PiBEZWNvZGUuZGVjb2RlU3RyaW5nIGJvb2tEZWNvZGVyIHw-IGRlc2NyaWJlIHw-IHByaW50Cg).
   Run `check` and read the `?titleDec` note: it has type `Decoder string` and suggests
   `Decode.string`. Fill both holes (`Decode.string`, `Decode.int`) and Run. The well-formed object
   becomes a typed `Book`, and the object missing `pages` becomes `failed (KeyError): 'pages'`.
2. Make the boundary-versus-engine point: the JSON is the untyped, failable edge, and decoding turns
   it into a `Book` or a structured error before the rest of the program sees it. Contrast with
   wrapping something like numpy, where Pyfun adds little because the speed lives in native code.
3. Open the [Lesson 13 exercise](https://simontreanor.github.io/Pyfun/playground/#code=bGV0IG11bHRpcGx5IGEgYiA9CiAgcmVzdWx0IHsKICAgIGxldCEgeCA9ID8KICAgIGxldCEgeSA9ID8KICAgIHJldHVybiB4ICogeQogIH0KCnByaW50IChtdWx0aXBseSAiNiIgIjciKQpwcmludCAobXVsdGlwbHkgIjYiICJub3BlIikK).
   Before filling it, show the staircase form from the top of lesson 13 (two nested `Result` matches)
   and point out that every `Error` branch does the same thing. Then fill the two holes with
   `Option.toResult "not a number" (String.toInt a)` and its `b` twin and Run.
4. Make the point that `let!` unwraps an `Ok`, `return` wraps the final value, and the short-circuit
   on the first `Error` is automatic. The `result { }` block is the staircase written once. (If you
   are splitting into six sessions, this is the break point.)
5. Open the [Lesson 14 exercise](https://simontreanor.github.io/Pyfun/playground/#code=bWVhc3VyZSBtCm1lYXN1cmUgcwoKbGV0IGRpc3RhbmNlID0gMjQwLjA8bT4KbGV0IGVsYXBzZWQgPSAzMC4wPHM-CgojIFNwZWVkIGlzIGRpc3RhbmNlIHBlciB1bml0IG9mIHRpbWUuIFRoaXMgbGluZSBkb2VzIG5vdCB0eXBlLWNoZWNrIHlldC4KbGV0IHNwZWVkID0gZGlzdGFuY2UgKyBlbGFwc2VkCgpwcmludCBzcGVlZAo).
   It adds a distance to a time. Run `check` and read the mismatch: `expected float<m>, found
   float<s>`. Change the `+` to `/` and Run to get `8.0`. Show the Python panel: the units are gone,
   the output is plain `distance / elapsed`. Units are checked, then erased.
6. Open the [Lesson 15 exercise](https://simontreanor.github.io/Pyfun/playground/#code=bGV0IGNUb0YgYyA9IGMgKiA5IC8vIDUgKyAzMgpsZXQgZlRvQyBmID0gKGYgLSAzMikgKiA1IC8vIDkKCnByaW50IChjVG9GIDEwMCkKcHJpbnQgKGZUb0MgMjEyKQo).
   Wrap the two functions in `module Temp =` and qualify the calls as `Temp.cToF` and `Temp.fToC`.
   Run. Note that this in-file module runs in the playground, while one-module-per-file projects need
   the installed compiler.
7. Finish with the capstone. Open the [Lesson 16 exercise](https://simontreanor.github.io/Pyfun/playground/#__KSAwLjA8bT4KICAgICAgbGV0IHRpbWUgPSBydW5zIHw-IExpc3QuZm9sZCAoZnVuIGEgciAtPiBhICsgci50aW1lICogMS4wPHM-KSAwLjA8cz4KICAgICAgbGV0IGF2ZyA9IGRpc3QgLyA_CiAgICAgIGYie25hbWVzfTogYXZlcmFnZSBzcGVlZCB7YXZnfSBtL3Mgb3ZlciB7TGlzdC5sZW4gcnVuc30gcnVucyIKICAgIGNhc2UgRXJyb3IgZTogZiJjb3VsZCBub3QgcmVhZCBpbnB1dCAoe2UuZXJyb3JLaW5kfSkiCgpwcmludCByZXBvcnQK).
   Run `check` and let the three hole notes name each type: `Decoder float`, `float<m>`, `float<'a>`.
   Fill them (`Decode.float`, `1.0<m>`, `time`) and Run to get the one-line report. Point at the join
   where JSON meets units: a decoded number is a plain `float`, and multiplying by `1.0<m>` lifts it
   into metres so the fold carries a `float<m>`.
8. Close the unit by naming what the capstone touched: types, matching, records, collections,
   decoding, computation expressions, units, and modules. Every piece the language showcases, in one
   small program that fails safely on bad input.

## Assigned exercises

- In class: the [Lesson 12 exercise](../learn/12-python-interop.md) and the
  [Lesson 13 exercise](../learn/13-computation-expressions.md), driven from the demo.
- Homework: the [Lesson 14 exercise](../learn/14-units-of-measure.md) and the
  [Lesson 15 exercise](../learn/15-modules.md).
- Capstone: the [Lesson 16 exercise](../learn/16-capstone.md), fill all three holes. Suitable as an
  in-class finale or a take-home assessment. As a stretch, ask students to feed the decoder a
  malformed JSON string and confirm the `Error` branch reports rather than crashes.

## Common misconceptions

- "`extern` means the Python call is safe now." Correction: `extern` gives the call a type, but the
  boundary is effectful by default and can still raise. Wrap a call that can fail in `try`, or decode
  the data, to turn failure into a value.
- "Decoding JSON is just `json.loads`." Correction: `json.loads` hands back an untyped shape.
  `Decode.decodeString` produces your record or a structured error, so the rest of the program never
  meets an untyped value.
- "`result { }` is a special block that runs differently at runtime." Correction: it desugars to the
  same `Result` short-circuit you would write by hand with nested matches. `let!` and `return` are
  sugar for bind and wrap.
- "Units of measure add runtime overhead to every number." Correction: units exist only during type
  checking and erase at lowering. The emitted Python is plain numbers.
- "A module changes how the code runs or performs." Correction: an in-file module is purely
  organizational namespacing. Members call each other by bare name inside, and you qualify them as
  `Module.member` from outside.

## Timing

- 10 min: recap the unit so far, then frame boundary versus engine.
- 20 min: demo steps 1 to 2 (extern and JSON decoding).
- 15 min: demo steps 3 to 4 (computation expressions).
- 15 min: demo steps 5 to 6 (units and modules).
- 20 min: demo steps 7 to 8 (the capstone) or students start it themselves.
- 10 min: unit wrap-up and pointers to the full course and playground.

=== chippenham.pyfun ===
# Direct trains from a station, grouped by destination — a Network Rail SCHEDULE
# feed turned into a readable Markdown timetable, with NO Python helper: the file
# is streamed, parsed, and rendered entirely in Pyfun.
#
#   cargo run -- run examples/interop/network-rail/chippenham.pyfun
#
# This is the boundary-vs-engine interop pattern taken to its limit — even the
# streaming boundary is Pyfun. The file object from `open`/`gzip.open` is consumed
# as a lazy `Seq string`, so a ~3 GB NDJSON snapshot streams in constant memory; a
# substring prefilter skips JSON parsing on the lines that can't match; and the
# `Decode` module turns each surviving line into typed data — no dict-poking, no
# bespoke Python. `open`/`gzip.open`'s mode + encoding and `write_text`'s encoding
# + newline are pinned as `extern` keyword arguments (see the externs below), so the Python
# call carries `encoding="utf-8"` without any positional filler.
#
# Runs out of the box against the bundled `sample.ndjson`. For the real feed
# (register at https://opendata.nationalrail.co.uk / Network Rail data feeds),
# point `dataFile` at your snapshot — the EXACT filename, `.json` or `.json.gz`
# (a `.gz` is detected by extension and streamed without decompressing).
#
# Performance: driving the ~20M-line loop through `Seq.fold` is correctness- and
# clarity-first, not throughput-first — expect a minute or two on the full feed
# (a native Python loop is faster, but that puts the hot path back in Python).
#
# STP caveat: counts reflect the day-of-week pattern of permanent + new schedules
# minus full cancellations (stp "C"), deduped by (departure, destination). A
# specific calendar date may differ. A full snapshot is all `Create` records, so
# transaction type isn't checked.

# `mode="rt"` opens the file as text and `encoding="utf-8"` reads UTF-8 instead of
# the platform locale (cp1252 on Windows) — both correct for the feed and ~5s
# faster on the full file. Pinning them as `extern` keyword arguments reaches
# `encoding` (a keyword-only / deep-positional arg) with no positional filler.
extern openText : string -> Seq string = builtins.open(mode="rt", encoding="utf-8")
extern gzipText : string -> Seq string = gzip.open(mode="rt", encoding="utf-8")
extern type Path
extern toPath : string -> Path = pathlib.Path
extern writeText : Path -> string -> int = pathlib.Path.write_text(encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")

type Stop = { tiploc: string, arr: string, dep: string }
type Run  = { uid: string, days: string, stp: string, stops: List Stop }
type Leg  = { dest: string, finalDest: string, rdays: string, depMin: int, arrMin: int, jt: int, via: List string }

let dataFile = "examples/interop/network-rail/sample.ndjson"
let outFile  = "examples/interop/network-rail/chippenham-routes.md"

# --- streaming boundary, in Pyfun: the file object is a lazy Seq of lines ---
let lines path =
  if String.endsWith ".gz" path then gzipText path else openText path

# --- decode the relevant lines into typed data (parse, don't validate) ---
let optStr key = Decode.oneOf [Decode.field key Decode.string, Decode.succeed ""]

let tipDec =
  Decode.field "TiplocV1"
    (Decode.map2 (fun c n -> (c, n))
      (Decode.field "tiploc_code" Decode.string)
      (optStr "tps_description"))

let stopDec =
  Decode.map3 (fun t a d -> (t, a, d))
    (Decode.field "tiploc_code" Decode.string)
    (optStr "public_arrival")
    (optStr "public_departure")

let schedDec =
  Decode.field "JsonScheduleV1"
    (Decode.map4 (fun uid days stp stops -> (uid, days, stp, stops))
      (Decode.field "CIF_train_uid" Decode.string)
      (optStr "schedule_days_runs")
      (optStr "CIF_stp_indicator")
      (Decode.field "schedule_segment" (Decode.field "schedule_location" (Decode.list stopDec))))

# Fold the lazy line Seq into (tiploc names, Chippenham-calling runs). A cheap
# substring test skips JSON parsing on the millions of lines that can't match —
# the same prefilter the Python did, now in Pyfun and in constant memory.
let ingest acc line =
  match acc:
    case (names, runs):
      if String.contains "TiplocV1" line then
        match Decode.decodeString tipDec line:
          case Ok (c, n): (Map.add c n names, runs)
          case Error _: acc
      else if String.contains "JsonScheduleV1" line and String.contains "CHIPNHM" line then
        match Decode.decodeString schedDec line:
          case Ok r: (names, List.concat runs [r])
          case Error _: acc
      else acc

let scan path = Seq.fold ingest (Map.empty, []) (lines path)

# --- shape the decoded tuples into typed records ---
let toStop t =
  match t:
    case (tp, a, d): Stop { tiploc = tp, arr = a, dep = d }

let toRun r =
  match r:
    case (uid, days, stp, stops):
      Run { uid = uid, days = days, stp = stp, stops = List.map toStop stops }

# A stop is a public calling point iff it advertises a public time.
let calls s = (s.arr != "" and s.arr != "0000") or (s.dep != "" and s.dep != "0000")

let toMin hhmm =
  match (String.toInt (String.slice 0 2 hhmm), String.toInt (String.slice 2 4 hhmm)):
    case (Some h, Some m): h * 60 + m
    case _: -1

let fmt2 n = if n < 10 then f"0{n}" else f"{n}"
let showTime m = f"{fmt2 (m // 60)}:{fmt2 (m % 60)}"

let jtime dep arr =
  let d = arr - dep
  if d < 0 then d + 1440 else d

let fromChippenham stops =
  match stops:
    case []: None
    case [s, *rest]:
      if s.tiploc == "CHIPNHM" and calls s then Some (s.dep, rest)
      else fromChippenham rest

let lastTiploc stops =
  match stops:
    case []: ""
    case [s]: s.tiploc
    case [_, *rest]: lastTiploc rest

let walkLegs days term depM via stops =
  match stops:
    case []: []
    case [s, *rest]:
      if calls s then
        let arrM = toMin s.arr
        let onward = List.concat via [s.tiploc]
        if arrM < 0 then walkLegs days term depM onward rest
        else
          let leg = Leg { dest = s.tiploc, finalDest = term, rdays = days, depMin = depM,
                          arrMin = arrM, jt = jtime depM arrM, via = via }
          List.concat [leg] (walkLegs days term depM onward rest)
      else walkLegs days term depM via rest

let legsOfRun r =
  if r.stp == "C" then []
  else
    match fromChippenham r.stops:
      case None: []
      case Some (chippDep, downstream):
        let depM = toMin chippDep
        if depM < 0 then []
        else walkLegs r.days (lastTiploc downstream) depM [] downstream

let runsOn day days = String.slice day (day + 1) days == "1"

let dedupLegs legs =
  let step acc leg =
    match acc:
      case (seen, out):
        let k = f"{leg.depMin}|{leg.dest}"
        match Map.tryFind k seen:
          case Some _: (seen, out)
          case None: (Map.add k true seen, List.concat out [leg])
  match List.fold step (Map.empty, []) legs:
    case (_, out): out

let groupByDest acc leg =
  Map.add leg.dest (List.concat (Option.withDefault [] (Map.tryFind leg.dest acc)) [leg]) acc

let insertByDep leg sorted =
  match sorted:
    case []: [leg]
    case [x, *rest]:
      if leg.depMin <= x.depMin then List.concat [leg] sorted
      else List.concat [x] (insertByDep leg rest)

let sortLegs legs = List.fold (fun acc l -> insertByDep l acc) [] legs

let minOf xs =
  match xs:
    case []: 0
    case [x]: x
    case [x, *rest]:
      let m = minOf rest
      if x < m then x else m

let maxOf xs =
  match xs:
    case []: 0
    case [x]: x
    case [x, *rest]:
      let m = maxOf rest
      if x > m then x else m

# --- title-casing (feed descriptions are UPPERCASE) ---
# Uppercase the first *alphabetic* char in a char list, leave the rest. The test
# `String.upper c != c` is true only for a lowercase letter, so "(south"
# capitalizes the s, not the "(".
let capFirst chars =
  match chars:
    case []: []
    case [c, *rest]:
      if String.upper c != c then List.concat [String.upper c] rest
      else List.concat [c] (capFirst rest)

let capWord w = String.join "" (capFirst (String.toList w))
let titleHyphen w = String.join "-" (List.map capWord (String.split "-" w))
let titleCase name = String.join " " (List.map titleHyphen (String.split " " (String.lower name)))

# --- rendering (Markdown) ---
let nameOf names tp = titleCase (Option.withDefault tp (Map.tryFind tp names))
let plural n word = if n == 1 then f"{n} {word}" else f"{n} {word}s"
let rangeStr lo hi = if lo == hi then f"{lo} min" else f"{lo}-{hi} min"

let renderService names leg =
  let stopStr =
    match leg.via:
      case []: "direct"
      case _:
        let viaStr = String.join ", " (List.map (nameOf names) leg.via)
        f"via {viaStr}"
  let onward = if leg.dest == leg.finalDest then "" else f" _(to {nameOf names leg.finalDest})_"
  f"- **{showTime leg.depMin} → {showTime leg.arrMin}** · {leg.jt} min · {stopStr}{onward}"

let renderGroup names g =
  match g:
    case (dest, legs):
      let times = List.map (fun l -> l.jt) legs
      let tr = plural (List.len legs) "train"
      let header = f"### {nameOf names dest} — {tr}, {rangeStr (minOf times) (maxOf times)}"
      let body = String.join "\n" (List.map (renderService names) (sortLegs legs))

# The SAME timetable as chippenham.pyfun, but the streaming boundary is a native
# Python loop (nr_stream.py) instead of a Pyfun `Seq.fold`. The domain engine below
# is byte-for-byte identical; only the I/O at the top differs.
#
#   cargo run -- compile examples/interop/network-rail/chippenham_fast.pyfun \
#       -o examples/interop/network-rail/chippenham_fast.py
#   PYTHONPATH=examples/interop/network-rail \
#       python examples/interop/network-rail/chippenham_fast.py
#
# Why keep this alongside the pure-Pyfun version? Because it's ~15x faster on the
# real feed (~5s vs ~75s for ~20M lines), and that gap is the whole lesson: the hot
# per-line loop belongs in a tight, C-backed Python `for` loop, not in a Pyfun fold
# that pays a call per element. Pyfun's job is the typed engine; Python's optimized
# libraries do the grinding. `extern` is the boundary that lets you have both —
# leverage the fast thing that already exists rather than re-emulate it in Pyfun.

extern scan: string -> ( (Map string string)
                       , (List ( string, string, string
                               , (List (string, string, string)) )) )
       = nr_stream.scan
extern writeUtf8: string -> string -> int = nr_stream.write_utf8

type Stop = { tiploc: string, arr: string, dep: string }
type Run  = { uid: string, days: string, stp: string, stops: List Stop }
type Leg  = { dest: string, finalDest: string, rdays: string, depMin: int, arrMin: int, jt: int, via: List string }

let dataFile = "examples/interop/network-rail/sample.ndjson"
let outFile  = "examples/interop/network-rail/chippenham-routes.md"

# --- shape the boundary's tuples into typed records ---
let toStop t =
  match t:
    case (tp, a, d): Stop { tiploc = tp, arr = a, dep = d }

let toRun r =
  match r:
    case (uid, days, stp, stops):
      Run { uid = uid, days = days, stp = stp, stops = List.map toStop stops }

# A stop is a public calling point iff it advertises a public time.
let calls s = (s.arr != "" and s.arr != "0000") or (s.dep != "" and s.dep != "0000")

let toMin hhmm =
  match (String.toInt (String.slice 0 2 hhmm), String.toInt (String.slice 2 4 hhmm)):
    case (Some h, Some m): h * 60 + m
    case _: -1

let fmt2 n = if n < 10 then f"0{n}" else f"{n}"
let showTime m = f"{fmt2 (m // 60)}:{fmt2 (m % 60)}"

let jtime dep arr =
  let d = arr - dep
  if d < 0 then d + 1440 else d

let fromChippenham stops =
  match stops:
    case []: None
    case [s, *rest]:
      if s.tiploc == "CHIPNHM" and calls s then Some (s.dep, rest)
      else fromChippenham rest

let lastTiploc stops =
  match stops:
    case []: ""
    case [s]: s.tiploc
    case [_, *rest]: lastTiploc rest

let walkLegs days term depM via stops =
  match stops:
    case []: []
    case [s, *rest]:
      if calls s then
        let arrM = toMin s.arr
        let onward = List.concat via [s.tiploc]
        if arrM < 0 then walkLegs days term depM onward rest
        else
          let leg = Leg { dest = s.tiploc, finalDest = term, rdays = days, depMin = depM,
                          arrMin = arrM, jt = jtime depM arrM, via = via }
          List.concat [leg] (walkLegs days term depM onward rest)
      else walkLegs days term depM via rest

let legsOfRun r =
  if r.stp == "C" then []
  else
    match fromChippenham r.stops:
      case None: []
      case Some (chippDep, downstream):
        let depM = toMin chippDep
        if depM < 0 then []
        else walkLegs r.days (lastTiploc downstream) depM [] downstream

let dedupLegs legs =
  let step acc leg =
    match acc:
      case (seen, out):
        let k = f"{leg.depMin}|{leg.dest}"
        match Map.tryFind k seen:
          case Some _: (seen, out)
          case None: (Map.add k true seen, List.concat out [leg])

    case (_, out): out

let groupByDest acc leg =
  Map.add leg.dest (List.concat (Option.withDefault [] (Map.tryFind leg.dest acc)) [leg]) acc

let insertByDep leg sorted =
  match sorted:
    case []: [leg]
    case [x, *rest]:
      if leg.depMin <= x.depMin then List.concat [leg] sorted
      else List.concat [x] (insertByDep leg rest)

let sortLegs legs = List.fold (fun acc l -> insertByDep l acc) [] legs

let minOf xs =
  match xs:
    case []: 0
    case [x]: x
    case [x, *rest]:
      let m = minOf rest
      if x < m then x else m

let maxOf xs =
  match xs:
    case []: 0
    case [x]: x
    case [x, *rest]:
      let m = maxOf rest
      if x > m then x else m

# --- title-casing (feed descriptions are UPPERCASE) ---
let capFirst chars =
  match chars:
    case []: []
    case [c, *rest]:
      if String.upper c != c then List.concat [String.upper c] rest
      else List.concat [c] (capFirst rest)

let titleHyphen w = String.join "-" (List.map capWord (String.split "-" w))
let titleCase name = String.join " " (List.map titleHyphen (String.split " " (String.lower name)))

let plural n word = if n == 1 then f"{n} {word}" else f"{n} {word}s"
let rangeStr lo hi = if lo == hi then f"{lo} min" else f"{lo}-{hi} min"

let renderService names leg =
  let stopStr =
    match leg.via:
      case []: "direct"
      case _:

  f"- **{showTime leg.depMin} → {showTime leg.arrMin}** · {leg.jt} min · {stopStr}{onward}"

      let tr = plural (List.len legs) "train"

      let body = String.join "\n" (List.map (renderService names) (sortLegs legs))

  let legs = dedupLegs (List.filter (fun l -> runsOn day l.rdays) allLegs)
  let pairs = List.map (fun g -> match g: case (dest, ls): (nameOf names dest, renderGroup names g))
                       (Map.toList (List.fold groupByDest Map.empty legs))
  let body = String.join "\n\n" (List.map (fun p -> match p: case (nm, txt): txt) (List.sort pairs))
  f"## {label}\n\n{body}"

let buildReport names raw =
  let allLegs = List.fold (fun acc r -> List.concat acc (legsOfRun r)) [] (List.map toRun raw)
  let intro = "# Direct services from Chippenham\n\n_Every station reachable directly (no change) from Chippenham, grouped by destination, in departure order. Counts reflect the weekly day-of-week pattern of permanent + new schedules minus cancellations; a specific date may differ._"
  let wd = daySection names "Monday–Friday (representative day: Tuesday)" 1 allLegs
  let sa = daySection names "Saturday" 5 allLegs
  let su = daySection names "Sunday" 6 allLegs
  String.join "\n\n" [intro, wd, sa, su]

let _ =
  match scan dataFile:
    case (names, raw): writeUtf8 outFile (buildReport names raw)

print (f"Wrote Markdown direct Chippenham services to {outFile}")

#
#   pyfun bundle examples/interop/browser/counter.pyfun -o site --page examples/interop/browser/counter.html
#   python -m http.server -d site     # then open http://localhost:8000/

# looks like. The state is a top-level `let mut` that the click handler
# reassigns (a `global` in the emitted Python); the handler is an ordinary Pyfun
# function whose one parameter is the event, handed to the page through
# `Dom.proxy`. No callback convention to remember: Python calls `bump(event)` with
# one argument, and that is the one parameter `bump` has.

let mut count = 0

  render ()

# datetime — the most-imported stdlib module, wrapped as typed, *pure* values.
#
#   pyfun run examples/interop/datetime.pyfun
#
# datetime is all classes, which makes it a tour of the object-side extern forms:
# a class target as a constructor, property/method receivers, and Python's
# `operator` module for the arithmetic the classes define with `+`/`-`. Building
# and combining dates is deterministic, so these externs are declared `pure` —
# the boundary's opt-out — and `let pure` then *proves* a whole pipeline effect-free.

extern type Datetime
extern type Delta

# A class is callable, so a class target is a constructor: `date 2026 7 13` lowers
# to datetime.datetime(2026, 7, 13), auto-importing the class's module.
extern pure date : int -> int -> int -> Datetime = datetime.datetime
extern pure days : int -> Delta = datetime.timedelta      # timedelta(days) — first positional

# Classmethods sit behind the *lowercase* class, which the import heuristic would
# read as a submodule — an `extern import` declares the module explicitly, exactly
# like Python's own import statement (DESIGN.md §6). `now` stays a plain (io)
# extern: a fresh value each call is an effect, and `let pure` over it would be a
# compile error; parsing a fixed string is pure.
extern import datetime
extern now : unit -> Datetime = datetime.datetime.now
extern pure parseIso : string -> Datetime = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat

# Members of the opaque handles: `= .attr` reads a property, `= .attr()` calls a method.
extern pure weekday   : Datetime -> int    = .weekday()   # 0 = Monday
extern pure isoformat : Datetime -> string = .isoformat()
extern pure inDays    : Delta -> int       = .days

# datetime's arithmetic lives on `+`/`-`, and Python exposes every operator as a
# plain function in the `operator` module — ready-made extern targets.
extern pure shift   : Datetime -> Delta -> Datetime = operator.add   # d + delta
extern pure between : Datetime -> Datetime -> Delta = operator.sub   # b - a

let launch = date 2026 7 13
print (isoformat launch)                                # 2026-07-13T00:00:00
print (weekday launch)                                  # 0 — a Monday
print (isoformat (parseIso "2026-07-13"))               # 2026-07-13T00:00:00

# `now` performs io, so `sinceLaunch` is inferred io — and prints nothing fixed.
let sinceLaunch = inDays (between (now ()) launch)

# The externs are pure, so the compiler verifies this pipeline touches no effect.
let pure daysBetween a b = inDays (between b a)
print (daysBetween launch (shift launch (days 90)))     # 90

# Boundary handles flow through the ordinary combinators like any other value.
let sprintEnds = List.map (fun n -> isoformat (shift launch (days (n * 14)))) [1, 2, 3]
print sprintEnds

# An impossible date raises ValueError in Python; `try` reifies it as a Result,
# and the match must handle both outcomes.
let describe r =
  match r:
    case Ok d: f"valid: {isoformat d}"
    case Error e: f"invalid: {e.errorKind}"

print (describe (try (date 2026 2 30)))                 # invalid: ValueError

# lowering. (`let pure shout n = print n` would be a compile error.)
let pure add a b = a + b

# `const : 'a -> 'b -> 'a`, `ignore : 'a -> unit`, `flip` swaps a function's

=== chippenham.pyfun ===
# Direct trains from a station, grouped by destination — a Network Rail SCHEDULE
# feed turned into a readable Markdown timetable, with NO Python helper: the file
# is streamed, parsed, and rendered entirely in Pyfun.
#
#   cargo run -- run examples/interop/network-rail/chippenham.pyfun
#
# This is the boundary-vs-engine interop pattern taken to its limit — even the
# streaming boundary is Pyfun. The file object from `open`/`gzip.open` is consumed
# as a lazy `Seq string`, so a ~3 GB NDJSON snapshot streams in constant memory; a
# substring prefilter skips JSON parsing on the lines that can't match; and the
# `Decode` module turns each surviving line into typed data — no dict-poking, no
# bespoke Python. `open`/`gzip.open`'s mode + encoding and `write_text`'s encoding
# + newline are pinned as `extern` keyword arguments (see the externs below), so the Python
# call carries `encoding="utf-8"` without any positional filler.
#
# Runs out of the box against the bundled `sample.ndjson`. For the real feed
# (register at https://opendata.nationalrail.co.uk / Network Rail data feeds),
# point `dataFile` at your snapshot — the EXACT filename, `.json` or `.json.gz`
# (a `.gz` is detected by extension and streamed without decompressing).
#
# Performance: driving the ~20M-line loop through `Seq.fold` is correctness- and
# clarity-first, not throughput-first — expect a minute or two on the full feed
# (a native Python loop is faster, but that puts the hot path back in Python).
#
# STP caveat: counts reflect the day-of-week pattern of permanent + new schedules
# minus full cancellations (stp "C"), deduped by (departure, destination). A
# specific calendar date may differ. A full snapshot is all `Create` records, so
# transaction type isn't checked.

# `mode="rt"` opens the file as text and `encoding="utf-8"` reads UTF-8 instead of
# the platform locale (cp1252 on Windows) — both correct for the feed and ~5s
# faster on the full file. Pinning them as `extern` keyword arguments reaches
# `encoding` (a keyword-only / deep-positional arg) with no positional filler.
extern openText : string -> Seq string = builtins.open(mode="rt", encoding="utf-8")
extern gzipText : string -> Seq string = gzip.open(mode="rt", encoding="utf-8")
extern type Path
extern toPath : string -> Path = pathlib.Path
extern writeText : Path -> string -> int = pathlib.Path.write_text(encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")

type Stop = { tiploc: string, arr: string, dep: string }
type Run  = { uid: string, days: string, stp: string, stops: List Stop }
type Leg  = { dest: string, finalDest: string, rdays: string, depMin: int, arrMin: int, jt: int, via: List string }

let dataFile = "examples/interop/network-rail/sample.ndjson"
let outFile  = "examples/interop/network-rail/chippenham-routes.md"

# --- streaming boundary, in Pyfun: the file object is a lazy Seq of lines ---
let lines path =
  if String.endsWith ".gz" path then gzipText path else openText path

# --- decode the relevant lines into typed data (parse, don't validate) ---
let optStr key = Decode.oneOf [Decode.field key Decode.string, Decode.succeed ""]

let tipDec =
  Decode.field "TiplocV1"
    (Decode.map2 (fun c n -> (c, n))
      (Decode.field "tiploc_code" Decode.string)
      (optStr "tps_description"))

let stopDec =
  Decode.map3 (fun t a d -> (t, a, d))
    (Decode.field "tiploc_code" Decode.string)
    (optStr "public_arrival")
    (optStr "public_departure")

let schedDec =
  Decode.field "JsonScheduleV1"
    (Decode.map4 (fun uid days stp stops -> (uid, days, stp, stops))
      (Decode.field "CIF_train_uid" Decode.string)
      (optStr "schedule_days_runs")
      (optStr "CIF_stp_indicator")

# A page that takes input: a counter with a button, running on Pyodide.
#
#   pyfun bundle examples/interop/browser/counter.pyfun -o site --page examples/interop/browser/counter.html
#   python -m http.server -d site     # then open http://localhost:8000/
#
# `Dom` is the typed façade in dom.pyfun; this program is what a consumer of it
# looks like. The state is a top-level `let mut` that the click handler
# reassigns (a `global` in the emitted Python); the handler is an ordinary Pyfun
# function whose one parameter is the event, handed to the page through
# `Dom.proxy`. No callback convention to remember: Python calls `bump(event)` with
# one argument, and that is the one parameter `bump` has.

import Dom

let mut count = 0

let render _ =
  Dom.setText (Dom.byId "count") f"{count}"

let bump _ =
  count <- count + 1
  render ()

Dom.on (Dom.byId "plus") "click" (Dom.proxy bump)
render ()
print "counter ready"
=== datetime.pyfun ===
# datetime — the most-imported stdlib module, wrapped as typed, *pure* values.
#
#   pyfun run examples/interop/datetime.pyfun
#
# datetime is all classes, which makes it a tour of the object-side extern forms:
# a class target as a constructor, property/method receivers, and Python's
# `operator` module for the arithmetic the classes define with `+`/`-`. Building
# and combining dates is deterministic, so these externs are declared `pure` —
# the boundary's opt-out — and `let pure` then *proves* a whole pipeline effect-free.

extern type Datetime
extern type Delta

# A class is callable, so a class target is a constructor: `date 2026 7 13` lowers
# to datetime.datetime(2026, 7, 13), auto-importing the class's module.
extern pure date : int -> int -> int -> Datetime = datetime.datetime
extern pure days : int -> Delta = datetime.timedelta      # timedelta(days) — first positional

# Classmethods sit behind the *lowercase* class, which the import heuristic would
# read as a submodule — an `extern import` declares the module explicitly, exactly
# like Python's own import statement (DESIGN.md §6). `now` stays a plain (io)
# extern: a fresh value each call is an effect, and `let pure` over it would be a
# compile error; parsing a fixed string is pure.
extern import datetime
extern now : unit -> Datetime = datetime.datetime.now
extern pure parseIso : string -> Datetime = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat

# Members of the opaque handles: `= .attr` reads a property, `= .attr()` calls a method.
extern pure weekday   : Datetime -> int    = .weekday()   # 0 = Monday
extern pure isoformat : Datetime -> string = .isoformat()
extern pure inDays    : Delta -> int       = .days

# datetime's arithmetic lives on `+`/`-`, and Python exposes every operator as a
# plain function in the `operator` module — ready-made extern targets.
extern pure shift   : Datetime -> Delta -> Datetime = operator.add   # d + delta
extern pure between : Datetime -> Datetime -> Delta = operator.sub   # b - a

let launch = date 2026 7 13
print (isoformat launch)                                # 2026-07-13T00:00:00
print (weekday launch)                                  # 0 — a Monday
print (isoformat (parseIso "2026-07-13"))               # 2026-07-13T00:00:00

# `now` performs io, so `sinceLaunch` is inferred io — and prints nothing fixed.
let sinceLaunch = inDays (between (now ()) launch)

# The externs are pure, so the compiler verifies this pipeline touches no effect.
let pure daysBetween a b = inDays (between b a)
print (daysBetween launch (shift launch (days 90)))     # 90

# Boundary handles flow through the ordinary combinators like any other value.
let sprintEnds = List.map (fun n -> isoformat (shift launch (days (n * 14)))) [1, 2, 3]
print sprintEnds

# An impossible date raises ValueError in Python; `try` reifies it as a Result,
# and the match must handle both outcomes.
let describe r =
  match r:
    case Ok d: f"valid: {isoformat d}"
    case Error e: f"invalid: {e.errorKind}"

print (describe (try (date 2026 2 30)))                 # invalid: ValueError

# A typed façade over the page, for a program that runs in the browser under
# Pyodide (`pyfun bundle`). Pyodide exposes the page as the `js` module, so the
# DOM is a set of externs like any other Python library; this module writes them
# once so a program imports them (`import Dom`) rather than repeating them.
#
# Every handle is opaque: the compiler follows an `Element` through the program
# without looking inside it. A callback handed to the page must be wrapped with
# `proxy` (Pyodide's `create_proxy`), which keeps it alive for as long as the page
# holds it; the façade is where that detail lives, not the program.

extern import js
extern import pyodide.ffi

extern type Element
extern type Event
extern type Callback

# The document, by id; a missing id raises at the boundary like any extern.
extern byId: string -> Element = js.document.getElementById

# Replace an element's children with one text node (`el.replaceChildren(text)`).
extern setText: Element -> string -> unit = .replaceChildren()

# `el.setAttribute(name, value)` and `el.append(child)`.
extern setAttr: Element -> string -> string -> unit = .setAttribute()
extern append: Element -> Element -> unit = .append()
extern create: string -> Element = js.document.createElement

# `el.addEventListener(event, callback)`; the callback performs `io` (it will).
extern on: Element -> string -> Callback -> unit = .addEventListener()
extern proxy: (Event ->{io} unit) -> Callback = pyodide.ffi.create_proxy

# A taste of the type-checked Phase 3 subset that compiles to runnable Python.
#   pyfun check   examples/hello.pyfun     (type-check)
#   pyfun compile examples/hello.pyfun     (emit Python)
#   pyfun run     examples/hello.pyfun     (run it)

# Algebraic data types: a plain enum. (`Option a = None | Some a` is built in.)
type Color = Red | Green | Blue

# Records: named-field product types (nominal; field names are unique).
type Point = { x: int, y: int }

# Curried function: inferred type int -> int -> int. `pure` is an opt-in
# assertion that the function performs no effects (no `io`); the compiler infers
# effects everywhere and only checks them where you ask. Effects are erased at
# lowering. (`let pure shout n = print n` would be a compile error.)
let pure add a b = a + b

# Partial application (functools.partial); full application (add(1, 4)).
let inc = add 1
let five = 4 |> inc

# Recursion is implicit: a function is in scope in its own body, like Python's
# `def` (no `rec` keyword). Deep recursion shares Python's stack limit; use the
# `List`/`Seq` combinators for stack-safe bulk work.
let fact n =
  if n == 0 then 1
  else n * fact (n - 1)

# Standard combinators are built in (`DESIGN.md` §6): `id : 'a -> 'a`,
# `const : 'a -> 'b -> 'a`, `ignore : 'a -> unit`, `flip` swaps a function's
# first two arguments. `flip` is effect-polymorphic; the rest are pure. (A user
# `let id x = x` would shadow the builtin, like any other prelude name.)
let same = id 42                       # 42
let always7 = const 7 "discarded"      # 7
let subtract a b = a - b
let backwards = flip subtract 3 10     # subtract 10 3 = 7
let zeroed = List.map (const 0) [1, 2, 3]   # [0, 0, 0]
let dropped = ignore 42                # unit (None) — ignore discards its argument

# Doc comments: a `##` line at column 0 attaches to the following top-level
# declaration as documentation (LSP hover shows it below the type), unlike an
# ordinary `#` comment. It erases at compile time.
## Returns 1 when the flag is set, else 0.
let pick b = if b then 1 else 0

# Multi-line doc comment: consecutive `##` lines join into one doc block (with
# `\n` between them), attached to the declaration that follows — here a `type`.
# This sum also shows the offside layout — one `| Variant` per line in an indented
# block after `=` (the F#/ML habit); `Color` above uses the inline `A | B | C`
# form. Both parse identically (a leading `|` is optional; the printer
# canonicalizes back to one line).
## A traffic signal.
## `Walk` when clear, `Wait` while it counts down, `Stop` otherwise. Ordered by
## declaration, so `Walk < Wait < Stop` under the derived comparison.
type Signal =
  | Walk
  | Wait
  | Stop

# Typed holes (shown as a comment — a hole blocks compilation by design, so this
# file can still `run`): write `?` or `?name` in expression position and the
# compiler reports the type it expects there — plus in-scope bindings that fit
# directly (`try:`) and functions whose result fits, applied to more holes
# (`or:`) — for type-driven development. E.g.
#     let use = String.concat ?g "!"
# makes `pyfun check` report `note: hole ?g has type string — try: greeting — or:
# String.upper ?, String.fromInt ?` and hover show it; `compile`/`run` refuse
# until it's filled. Fill inward from the types (and the suggested fits).

# Blocks: an indented body is a sequence of statements ending in the value. They
# open after `=` (a `let` body), `->` (a lambda), `case P:` (a `match` arm), `then`/`else`.
# `let mut` + `<-` give local mutation; reassigning a plain `let` is a compile
# error (immutable by default). Lowers to a flat Python statement sequence.
let scaled a b =
  let mut acc = a
  acc <- acc + b
  acc <- acc * 2
  acc

# A closure that reassigns a captured `mut` — `tally` mutates `running` across
# calls. The compiler emits Python's `nonlocal`/`global` so the capture is correct
# (F# auto-boxes a captured mutable into a reference cell; same idea).
let accumulate =
  let mut running = 0
  let tally x =
    running <- running + x
    running
  let first = tally 10
  tally 5                             # 15  (10 then +5)

# A block in a `match` arm (opened after `case P:`).
let describeSign n =
  match n:
    case 0: "zero"
    case _:
        let positive = n > 0
        if positive then "positive" else "negative"

# Exhaustive pattern matching over an ADT (checked at compile time).
let unwrap o =
  match o:
    case Some v: v
    case None: 0

let answer = unwrap (Some 42)

# An as-pattern (`p as x`) binds the whole matched value alongside destructuring —
# and it's transparent to the exhaustiveness check (`Some v as w` covers Some).
let doubleIfSome o =
  match o:
    case Some v as w: w
    case None: None
let stillFortyTwo = doubleIfSome (Some 42)   # Some 42

let rank c =
  match c:
    case Red: 1
    case Green: 2
    case Blue: 3

# This is the boundary-vs-engine interop pattern taken to its limit — even the
# streaming boundary is Pyfun. The file object from `open`/`gzip.open` is consumed
# as a lazy `Seq string`, so a ~3 GB NDJSON snapshot streams in constant memory; a
# substring prefilter skips JSON parsing on the lines that can't match; and the
# `Decode` module turns each surviving line into typed data — no dict-poking, no
# bespoke Python. `open`/`gzip.open`'s mode + encoding and `write_text`'s encoding
# + newline are pinned as `extern` keyword arguments (see the externs below), so the Python
# call carries `encoding="utf-8"` without any positional filler.
#

# (a `.gz` is detected by extension and streamed without decompressing).

# clarity-first, not throughput-first — expect a minute or two on the full feed

results.content:
1	# A taste of the type-checked Phase 3 subset that compiles to runnable Python.
2	#   pyfun check   examples/hello.pyfun     (type-check)
3	#   pyfun compile examples/hello.pyfun     (emit Python)
4	#   pyfun run     examples/hello.pyfun     (run it)
5	
6	# Algebraic data types: a plain enum. (`Option a = None | Some a` is built in.)
7	type Color = Red | Green | Blue
8	
9	# Records: named-field product types (nominal; field names are unique).
10	type Point = { x: int, y: int }
11	
12	# Curried function: inferred type int -> int -> int. `pure` is an opt-in
13	# assertion that the function performs no effects (no `io`); the compiler infers
14	# effects everywhere and only checks them where you ask. Effects are erased at
15	# lowering. (`let pure shout n = print n` would be a compile error.)
16	let pure add a b = a + b
17	
18	# Partial application (functools.partial); full application (add(1, 4)).
19	let inc = add 1
20	let five = 4 |> inc
21	
22	# Recursion is implicit: a function is in scope in its own body, like Python's
23	# `def` (no `rec` keyword). Deep recursion shares Python's stack limit; use the
24	# `List`/`Seq` combinators for stack-safe bulk work.
25	let fact n =
26	  if n == 0 then 1
27	  else n * fact (n - 1)
28	
29	# Standard combinators are built in (`DESIGN.md` §6): `id : 'a -> 'a`,
30	# `const : 'a -> 'b -> 'a`, `ignore : 'a -> unit`, `flip` swaps a function's
31	# first two arguments. `flip` is effect-polymorphic; the rest are pure. (A user
32	# `let id x = x` would shadow the builtin, like any other prelude name.)
33	let same = id 42                       # 42
34	let always7 = const 7 "discarded"      # 7
35	let subtract a b = a - b
36	let backwards = flip subtract 3 10     # subtract 10 3 = 7
37	let zeroed = List.map (const 0) [1, 2, 3]   # [0, 0, 0]
38	let dropped = ignore 42                # unit (None) — ignore discards its argument
39	
40	# Doc comments: a `##` line at column 0 attaches to the following top-level
41	# declaration as documentation (LSP hover shows it below the type), unlike an
42	# ordinary `#` comment. It erases at compile time.
43	## Returns 1 when the flag is set, else 0.
44	let pick b = if b then 1 else 0
45	
46	# Multi-line doc comment: consecutive `##` lines join into one doc block (with
47	# `\n` between them), attached to the declaration that follows — here a `type`.
48	# This sum also shows the offside layout — one `| Variant` per line in an indented
49	# block after `=` (the F#/ML habit); `Color` above uses the inline `A | B | C`
50	# form. Both parse identically (a leading `|` is optional; the printer
51	# canonicalizes back to one line).
52	## A traffic signal.
53	## `Walk` when clear, `Wait` while it counts down, `Stop` otherwise. Ordered by
54	## declaration, so `Walk < Wait < Stop` under the derived comparison.
55	type Signal =
56	  | Walk
57	  | Wait
58	  | Stop
59	
60	# Typed holes (shown as a comment — a hole blocks compilation by design, so this
61	# file can still `run`): write `?` or `?name` in expression position and the
62	# compiler reports the type it expects there — plus in-scope bindings that fit
63	# directly (`try:`) and functions whose result fits, applied to more holes
64	# (`or:`) — for type-driven development. E.g.
65	#     let use = String.concat ?g "!"
66	# makes `pyfun check` report `note: hole ?g has type string — try: greeting — or:
67	# String.upper ?, String.fromInt ?` and hover show it; `compile`/`run` refuse
68	# until it's filled. Fill inward from the types (and the suggested fits).
69	
70	# Blocks: an indented body is a sequence of statements ending in the value. They
71	# open after `=` (a `let` body), `->` (a lambda), `case P:` (a `match` arm), `then`/`else`.
72	# `let mut` + `<-` give local mutation; reassigning a plain `let` is a compile
73	# error (immutable by default). Lowers to a flat Python statement sequence.
74	let scaled a b =
75	  let mut acc = a
76	  acc <- acc + b
77	  acc <- acc * 2
78	  acc
79	
80	# A closure that reassigns a captured `mut` — `tally` mutates `running` across
81	# calls. The compiler emits Python's `nonlocal`/`global` so the capture is correct
82	# (F# auto-boxes a captured mutable into a reference cell; same idea).
83	let accumulate =
84	  let mut running = 0
85	  let tally x =
86	    running <- running + x
87	    running
88	  let first = tally 10
89	  tally 5                             # 15  (10 then +5)
90	
91	# A block in a `match` arm (opened after `case P:`).
92	let describeSign n =
93	  match n:
94	    case 0: "zero"
95	    case _:
96	        let positive = n > 0
97	        if positive then "positive" else "negative"
98	
99	# Exhaustive pattern matching over an ADT (checked at compile time).
100	let unwrap o =
101	  match o:
102	    case Some v: v
103	    case None: 0
104	
105	let answer = unwrap (Some 42)
106	
107	# An as-pattern (`p as x`) binds the whole matched value alongside destructuring —
108	# and it's transparent to the exhaustiveness check (`Some v as w` covers Some).
109	let doubleIfSome o =
110	  match o:
111	    case Some v as w: w
112	    case None: None
113	let stillFortyTwo = doubleIfSome (Some 42)   # Some 42
114	
115	let rank c =
116	  match c:
117	    case Red: 1
118	    case Green: 2
119	    case Blue: 3
120	
121	# Mutual recursion works implicitly (no `rec`/`and`): `isEven` sees `isOdd` and
122	# vice versa, defined in either order.
123	let isEven n = if n == 0 then true else isOdd (n - 1)
124	let isOdd n = if n == 0 then false else isEven (n - 1)
125	let tenEven = isEven 10               # true
126	
127	# Or-patterns: `case a | b:` matches any alternative (Python-identical). All
128	# alternatives must bind the same variables (here, none).
129	let size n =
130	  match n:
131	    case 1 | 2 | 3: "small"
132	    case _: "big"
133	
134	# Guards: a `case` arm may carry an `if` condition. A guarded arm is refutable —
135	# it never counts toward exhaustiveness, so a catch-all `case _` is still needed.
136	let sign n =
137	  match n:
138	    case 0: "zero"
139	    case m if m > 0: "positive"
140	    case _: "negative"
141	
142	# `elif` — sugar for `else if`; `if`/`then`/`else` stay (an inline expression, not
143	# `:`-framed). The printer canonicalizes any else-if chain to `elif`.
144	let grade n =
145	  if n >= 90 then "A"
146	  elif n >= 80 then "B"
147	  elif n >= 70 then "C"
148	  else "F"
149	
150	# Higher-order composition: ('b -> 'c) -> ('a -> 'b) -> 'a -> 'c.
151	let compose = fun f g x -> f (g x)
152	let inc2 = compose inc inc
153	let seven = inc2 five
154	
155	# Function composition operators: `>>` is left-to-right (f then g), `<<` is
156	# right-to-left (math ∘). Tighter than `|>`, so `x |> f >> g` = `x |> (f >> g)`.
157	let twice x = x * 2
158	let incThenDouble = inc >> twice
159	let doubleThenInc = inc << twice
160	let eight = incThenDouble 3            # twice (inc 3) = 8
161	let sevenC = doubleThenInc 3           # inc (twice 3) = 7
162	# Backward pipe `<|` applies a function to an argument (F#'s `<|`), dropping parens
163	# on the right: `inc <| twice 3` = `inc (twice 3)`. Right-associative.
164	let sevenB = inc <| twice 3            # inc (twice 3) = 7
165	
166	# In-file modules: a namespace of `let` bindings. Members see each other
167	# unqualified inside (`area` calls `square`); outside they are `Geom.member`.
168	module Geom =
169	  let square x = x * x
170	  let area w h = w * h
171	  let diagSq w h = square w + square h
172	let floorArea = Geom.area 4 5         # 20
173	let diag = Geom.diagSq 3 4            # 25
174	
175	# Computation expressions (F# showcase features):
176	#   result {} — railway-oriented, short-circuits on Error (built-in Ok/Error).
177	let checked ok v =
178	  result {
179	    let! x = if ok then Ok v else Error 0
180	    return x + 1
181	  }
182	
183	#   option {} — the same railway over Option, for chaining lookups that may find
184	#   nothing. One `case None` arm covers the whole chain instead of one per step.
185	let firstTwo xs =
186	  option {
187	    let! a = List.get 0 xs
188	    let! b = List.get 1 xs
189	    return a + b
190	  }
191	print (firstTwo [10, 20, 30])      # Some(30)
192	print (firstTwo [10])              # None_ — the emitted class name, `None` being taken in Python
193	
194	#   seq {} — a lazy sequence, lowered to a Python generator.
195	let small =
196	  seq {
197	    yield 1
198	    yield 2
199	    yield 3
200	  }
201	
202	#   async {} — lowered to a Python coroutine (async def / await). A coroutine must be
203	#   awaited somewhere, so run one to a value with an `extern` over `asyncio.run`.
204	extern runAsync: Async a -> a = asyncio.run
205	let computed =
206	  async {
207	    let! x = async { return 20 }
208	    return x + 1
209	  }
210	print (runAsync computed)          # 21
211	
212	# User-defined CE builders: any in-file `module` providing `bind`/`return_` (and
213	# `yield_`/`combine`/`delay`/… for sequence builders) is a builder. `Maybe { … }`
214	# desugars to `Maybe.bind`/`Maybe.return_` calls — ordinary inference does the rest.
215	module Maybe =
216	  let bind m f =
217	    match m:
218	      case Some x: f x
219	      case None: None
220	  let return_ x = Some x
221	let addOpt a b =
222	  Maybe {
223	    let! x = a
224	    let! y = b
225	    return x + y
226	  }
227	
228	# Tuples: structural (anonymous) products, `(a, b, c)`. `()` is unit and `(x)` is
229	# grouping, so a tuple has two or more elements. They lower ~1:1 to Python tuples
230	# and destructure in `match` (a single variable pattern is exhaustive).
231	let pairUp a b = (a, b)
232	let origin = (0, 0)

origin\nprint (describe here)                 # elsewhere\n\n# List/sequence patterns in `match` over a `List`: `[]`, a fixed `[x]`, and a\n# `*rest` star that may sit ANYWHERE (Python's one-star rule) — `[x, *rest]`\n# (head + tail), `[*init, last]` (all but the last), `[a, *mid, z]` (first and\n# last, middle bound). `[]` plus a star arm is exhaustive.\nlet shape xs =\n  match xs:\n    case []: \"empty\"\n    case [only]: \"one\"\n    case [a, *mid, z]: \"first and last, some middle\"\nlet lastOf xs =\n  match xs:\n    case []: 0\n    case [*init, last]: last\nprint (shape [1, 2, 3, 4])            # first and last, some middle\nprint (shape [7])                     # one\nprint (lastOf [10, 20, 30])           # 30  (non-last star: [*init, last])\n\n# Externs in action (call out to Python's str / math.fabs).\nprint label                           # 42\nprint root                            # 3.0\n\n# `try` in action: recover a default, and read the caught exception's kind.\nprint parsed42                        # 42\nprint parsedBad                       # 0    (try caught the ValueError)\nprint (errorKindOf \"nope\")            # ValueError\n\n# Lists in action.\nprint squares                         # [1, 4, 9, 16, 25]\nprint bigs                            # [3, 4, 5]\nprint total                           # 15\nprint count                           # 5\nprint product                         # 120                  (`(*)` section)\nprint doubled                         # [2, 4, 6, 8, 10]     (`(*) 2` section)\nprint third                           # 3    (List.get, O(1), total via Option)\nprint hasThree                        # True (List.contains, O(n))\nprint joined                          # [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]  (List.concat)\nprint ordered                         # [1, 2, 3]  (List.sort, O(n log n))\nprint sortedColors                    # [Red, Green, Blue]  (derived ADT ordering)\nprint sortedOpts                      # [None_, Some(1), Some(3)]  (Option orders)\nprint redFirst                        # True\nprint firstBig                        # Some(4)  (List.find, first match)\n\n# Sets, maps, and options in action.\nprint (Set.len uniq)                  # 3\nprint ada                             # 10\nprint nobody                          # 0\nprint doubled                         # Some(20)  (Option.bind)\nprint bigScore                        # None_     (Option.filter, 9 <= 9)\nprint adaOrErr                        # Ok(10)    (Option.toResult)\nprint adaAge                          # 36   (zip -> Map.ofList -> tryFind)\nprint entries                         # [('ada', 36), ('alan', 41)]\n\n# Strings in action.\nprint loud                            # HELLO, WORLD\nprint words                           # ['Hello', 'World']\nprint csv                             # Hello,World\nprint sub                             # Hello  (String.slice, total)\nprint commaAt                         # 5      (String.tryIndexOf -> Option int)\nprint (String.len title)             # 12\nprint parsed                          # 41   (total parse of \"41\")\nprint unparsed                        # 0    (String.toInt \"x\" -> None)\nprint cafeLen                         # 4    (UTF-8 \"café\" is 4 characters)\nprint emojiLen                        # 4    (\\u{1F600} is one character)\nprint winPath                         # C:\\Users\\pyfun   (raw string)\nprint rawLen                          # 4    (r\"a\\nb\" is 4 literal characters)\nprint scoreLine                       # Ada scored 41 (ADA)   (f-string)\nprint sumLine                         # 41 doubled is 82\nprint debugLine                       # parsed=41             (f-string `{x=}`)\nprint banner                          # two lines: == pyfun == / a \"quoted\" word\nprint summary                         # two lines: who: Ada / score: 41\nprint (String.len rawBlock)           # B\nprint (grade 68)                      # F\n\n# A user-defined computation expression (the Maybe monad).\nprint (addOpt (Some 3) (Some 4))      # Some(7)\nprint (addOpt (Some 3) None)          # None_  (short-circuits)\n\n# Tuples: construction, destructuring, and the Python tuple they become.\nprint (pairUp 1 2)                     # A total pattern (|A|B|) is a closed case set, so its match\n# needs no `_`; a partial pattern (|A|_|) returns Option (the case binds the\n# payload) or bool (a pure predicate, binds nothing) and needs a fallthrough.\nlet (|Even|Odd|) n = if n % 2 == 0 then Even else Odd\nlet parity n =\n  match n:\n    case Even: \"even\"\n    case Odd: \"odd\"\n\nlet (|Positive|_|) n = if n > 0 then Some n else None\nlet clamped n =\n  match n:\n    case Positive p: p\n    case _: 0\n\nlet (|Blank|_|) s = String.strip s == \"\"\nlet lineKind s =\n  match s:\n    case Blank: \"empty\"\n    case _: \"text\"\n\nprint (parity 4)                      # even\nprint (parity 7)                      # odd\nprint (clamped 9)                     # 9\nprint (clamped (0 - 5))               # 0\nprint (lineKind \"   \")                # empty\nprint (lineKind \"hi\")                 # text\n", "numLines": 647, "startLine": 1, "totalLines": 647}}
